user.title: Connect to Amber
user.description: Enter an Amber API key. You can create one on Amber's developer page.

site.title: Choose a site
site.description: Each site is set up as its own entry.

channels.title: Confirm channels
channels.description:
These metering channels were found for NMI {nmi}. Usage, cost and feed-in compensation will be imported for each of them.

{channels}

schedule.title: Import schedule
schedule.description: Amber publishes usage about a day late. Automatic picks a stable time for this installation each morning (between 06:30 and 08:30), with retries 3 and 6 hours later. Once the day is imported, the remaining attempts are skipped.

data_description.fixed_times: Only for fixed times: up to 6 local times, comma separated, for example 07:15, 10:15, 13:15.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Amber
reauth_confirm.description: Amber rejected the API key for NMI {nmi}. Enter a new key for the same account.

settings.title: Import schedule
settings.description: Automatic picks a stable time each morning (between 06:30 and 08:30), with retries 3 and 6 hours later.

data_description.fixed_times: Only for fixed times: up to 6 local times, comma separated, for example 07:15, 10:15, 13:15.
data_description.patience_days: A day that stays empty on this many separate days, while later days have data, is skipped as a gap (default 7).
data_description.revision_days: Days with estimated data are re-checked daily for this many days; if Amber revises them, history is rewritten from that day on (default 14, 0 turns it off).
data_description.usage_mode: Full imports usage every day. Recovery-only imports nothing on a schedule (use the backfill service). Pricing-only writes no usage statistics, only prices and own-sensor cost. Switching never deletes statistics; ones no longer updated simply stop.
data_description.price_series: Also write an hourly price series per channel (AUD/kWh). An hourly mean price is not a cost rate. Enabling it fetches the full retention window once (about 13 API calls for 90 days).
data_description.own_fallback: When 5-minute sensor data is no longer available (after about 10 days), price hourly energy at the hour's mean price and flag the day as lower precision. If off, such days are skipped.

migrate_pick.title: Choose the legacy statistics
migrate_pick.description:
{reason}

Pick the statistics your YAML kit wrote. Only the grid import is required; statistics are never mixed with a detected layout.

data_description.export_cost: The migration works out the sign from the days both the kit and this integration have.

migrate_confirm.title: Migrate from the YAML kit: dry run

data.confirm_backup: I have a current Home Assistant backup

data_description.confirm_backup: Required. Nothing has been changed yet; submitting runs the migration.

migrate_flagged.title: Migrate from the YAML kit: implausible legacy rows

data.exclude_flagged: Leave the flagged rows out and re-derive the sums around them

data_description.exclude_flagged: Nothing has been changed yet. Ticked: a new dry run without those rows is shown before anything runs. Not ticked: the migration stops.

undo_migration.title: Undo migration
undo_migration.description: Restores the Energy dashboard settings saved before the migration, and turns back on only the automations the migration turned off. Copied history and the re-based sums stay.

error.invalid_times: Enter one to six times as HH:MM, separated by commas.
error.backup_not_confirmed: Confirm that you have a current Home Assistant backup.

abort.not_loaded: The integration is not loaded; migration and undo need it running.

marker_mismatch.title: Amber import stopped: marker and statistics disagree
marker_mismatch.description:
The import for {entry} has stopped because its saved position does not match the statistics in the database: {details}.

Nothing has been written. This can happen if statistics were changed or deleted by hand, or the integration's storage was restored from a different backup. Restore a consistent backup, or open an issue with the diagnostics attached.

unexpected_channel.title: Amber reports a new metering channel
unexpected_channel.description:
Usage for {day} on {entry} contains a channel that is not configured: {details}.

This usually means a new meter channel (for example controlled load) was added to your Amber account. Imports are paused so that no data is lost or mis-assigned. Open the integration and choose **Reconfigure** to add the channel; imports then continue from {day}.

incomplete_data.title: Amber usage data is incomplete
incomplete_data.description:
Usage for {day} on {entry} failed the completeness check ({reason}): {details}.

Nothing was written for this day. The next attempt will fetch it again; this clears automatically once a complete day is imported.

import_failed.title: Amber import could not be verified
import_failed.description:
{day} was written for {entry} but reading it back did not match: {details}.

The import position was not advanced. The next attempt will rewrite the day.

behind.title: Amber import is behind
behind.description:
After the last scheduled attempt today, {entry} has only reached {last_date} ({days_behind} days behind yesterday). Last run: {status} {reason}

This clears by itself once the import catches up. If it persists for several days, check the status sensor and diagnostics.

legacy_cleanup.title: Finish removing the YAML kit ({entry})

import_day.name: Import day
import_day.description: Import one NEM day of Amber usage and cost into statistics. Only the day after the latest imported day, or the latest imported day itself, can be imported.

date.name: Date
date.description: The NEM date (Australian Eastern Standard Time) to import.

config_entry_id.name: Site
config_entry_id.description: The Amber site to import for. Optional when only one site is configured.

run_now.name: Run now
run_now.description: Catch up now: import every missing day up to yesterday, as a scheduled run would.

config_entry_id.name: Site
config_entry_id.description: The Amber site to run for. Optional when only one site is configured.

probe_retention.name: Probe retention
probe_retention.description: Discover Amber's usage retention boundary again from scratch (at most 8 API calls), instead of waiting for the daily check. The stored boundary is kept if the probe fails.

config_entry_id.name: Site
config_entry_id.description: The Amber site. Optional when only one site is configured.

backfill.name: Backfill
backfill.description: Import a range of NEM days on demand (Recovery-only mode, or to fill history before the first imported day). Days older than Amber's retention are skipped; a range before existing data rewrites the later sums.

end_date.name: End date
end_date.description: Last NEM date to import (at most yesterday).

config_entry_id.name: Site
config_entry_id.description: The Amber site. Optional when only one site is configured.

migrate_v1.name: Migrate from the YAML kit
migrate_v1.description: Dry run (default) or run the migration from the v1 kit or the advanced YAML version: parity check, copy of older history, Energy dashboard switch and legacy automations turned off. Take a Home Assistant backup first.

dry_run.name: Dry run
dry_run.description: Only report what would happen (default on).

confirm_backup.name: Backup confirmed
confirm_backup.description: Required for a real run: you have a current Home Assistant backup.

exclude_flagged.name: Leave out implausible rows
exclude_flagged.description: Leave out legacy rows the scan flags as implausible (such as a 99999 test spike) and re-derive the sums around them. Without it, flagged rows stop a real run.

import_energy.name: Grid import kWh
import_energy.description: Legacy grid import statistic (only when the kit is not detected automatically).

export_cost.name: Export cost
export_cost.description: Legacy export cost or compensation statistic (manual pick).

config_entry_id.name: Site
config_entry_id.description: The Amber site. Optional when only one site is configured.

undo_migration.name: Undo migration
undo_migration.description: Restore the Energy dashboard settings saved by the migration and turn back on the automations it turned off. Copied history stays.

config_entry_id.name: Site
config_entry_id.description: The Amber site. Optional when only one site is configured.

delete_legacy_statistics.name: Delete legacy statistics
delete_legacy_statistics.description: After a completed migration, permanently delete the YAML kit's statistics. The migration can no longer be undone afterwards.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be on; the deletion cannot be reversed.

config_entry_id.name: Site
config_entry_id.description: The Amber site. Optional when only one site is configured.

user.title: Price your own energy sensor
user.description: Choose a cumulative energy sensor (for example CT clamps or a smart plug) and the Amber channel whose billed price applies. Its cost is recorded as a statistic, from the later of the sensor's history start and Amber's retention boundary.

error.not_cumulative_energy: Choose a sensor with device class energy and state class total or total_increasing.
